## Table S10. Nested validation of the termination hazard model

(a) Out-of-sample performance of the adjustment-only model (log event age, day of the season, same-day national Tmin anomaly, winter start year) and of the model that adds the predictors selected within each training fold. In every fold, predictors were standardized with training data only, each of the 39 causal primary-family candidates was tested with a likelihood-ratio test, Benjamini–Hochberg q < 0.05 was applied, the diurnal temperature range was excluded (it is algebraically redundant with Tmax once Tmin is adjusted for), and candidates correlated at |r| > 0.8 with a stronger selected predictor were skipped. Folds are single winters with at least one spell (leave-one-winter-out) or the two halves of the record. ΔAUC and ΔBrier are the selected minus the adjustment-only model, with 95% winter-block bootstrap intervals; Brier skill is relative to the training-fold event frequency; the calibration slope and the ratio of observed to expected terminations refer to the held-out predictions. In the split-period folds the winter-start-year term is extrapolated beyond the training period; trained on the later half, even the adjustment-only model scores worse than the training-period climatology (Brier 0.307 against 0.218), and calibration is poor in both directions. (b) Predictors selected in the training folds. This table supersedes Table S7, in which the predictors had been chosen on the full record. The AUC values are plotted in Fig. S1b.

## Table S13. Robustness of the deficit of cold-spell onsets after major sudden stratospheric warmings

Cold-spell onsets within each window after the 25 major SSWs of 1985/86–2024/25 (Table S1). Null rows compare the observed count with control dates moved to the same calendar date in randomly chosen other winters (calendar-matched) or in winters within five winters of the SSW winter (decade-matched), 10,000 replicates each, redrawing any control date within 45 days of a real SSW; the ratio is observed over expected onsets, the range is the 2.5–97.5 percentile range of the null, and Monte Carlo p-values are two-sided. The ratio per at-risk day divides onsets by at-risk winter days (days not inside an ongoing spell after its first day) in both the observed and the control windows. Onset-rate rows compare onsets per at-risk day after SSWs with all other at-risk DJF days, or with the rest of the winters that contain the SSWs, with exact conditional binomial 95% intervals. SSWs in March have no December–February follow-up. The ENSO-phase-matched null (6 onsets against 15.9 expected) is reported in the main text.
